newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- finishes up 1/8 to 1/4 pt.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- finishes up 1/8 to 1/4 pt.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds reversed early losses Wednesday, ending a quiet session up about 1/8 to 1/4 point, traders said.
The market tracked Treasury prices throughout the day, moving back to unchanged at midday and then higher in late trading.
The government long bond was up 14/32 at 99-6/32 to yield 6.69 percent, after the Federal Reserve's Beige Book, released at 1400 EDT, said there are "pockets of weakness" in the U.S. economy.
The report also said labor markets are tight, but are still showing little or no signs of wage pressure.
Muni traders said secondary activity was light, with attention focused on a large slate of new issue pricings.

On the competitive side, Lehman Brothers said it won $200 million Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority bonds at a true interest cost of 5.392 percent. The firm reoffered the 2023 term bonds at a 5.45 percent yield, and did not formally reoffer the 2027 maturity.
In late day repricings, Bear Stearns & Co. said it repriced a $133 million Michigan Municipal Bond Authority deal, raising yields in several maturities but leaving the top yield unchanged.
Debt futures also reversed early losses to finish the day in positive territory.

September municipal futures rose 10/32 to 118-10/32, while September Treasury futures rose 9/32 to 112-5/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 197 ticks from 196 at the close on Tuesday.
In secondary trading, bids on Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up 1/8 at 101-1/8. Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were up 1/8 to 101-1/4.
